Hmm, but is that right? If sign is a label (σ_i→−σ_i), then NP is also invariant under relabeling... So how can AF break NP while FM keeps it? Because NP is about the *field* ordering: relabeling σ_i→−σ_i maps the operator to one with thresholds' α↔β swapped, i.e., the field direction is reversed for that element. NP requires a consistent partial order over the *field* axis; reversing one element's state label reverses its field ordering, so the global partial order (monotone in H) fails. So: sign is a label only if you also allow redefining which direction of H is "up" for that element — which you cannot do globally when elements are driven by a *common* field H. Ah, that's the crux! In a common-field drive, all elements see the same γ; flipping a label reverses that element's *orientation relative to H*, which is not a symmetry of the driven system because H is external and common. Hence: the gauge is a symmetry of the *undriven* energy/transition-graph, but not of the driven response ordering (NP/Preisach). That's a genuinely sharp distinction and it *revises* my v4 assumption: b→−b is a label change preserving ρ? Wait — earlier I argued ρ (release order along main loop) is preserved. Is that consistent? If flipping labels reverses one element's orientation to H, then its release order along the sweep would reverse → ρ would change. Hmm. Let me think concretely.

Element i with thresholds for up-switch at α_i(σ_j) and down-switch at β_i(σ_j), α_i > β_i. Relabel σ_i→−σ_i: the "up" transition becomes "down" and thresholds swap: new α' = −β_i, β' = −α_i. The release *positions* on the H axis: the element switches at H = α when going up, at H = β when going down. After relabeling, its switching events occur at the same physical H values but their up/down identity is swapped, so the sequence of states (with the new label) along the loop is the same. So ρ (the permutation/order of state changes of elements along the loop) — the *event ordering* is unchanged; only the direction label of the element's own transition is swapped. So a system where the element's + state is at small H vs large H differs only in which label. But the partial ordering property NP concerns: for two elements i,j, whether their states are ordered (e.g., if s_i=+ then s_j=+) monotonically in H. Relabeling one element inverts the meaning of that element's state, which can convert "monotone increasing" into "monotone decreasing" between i and j → so pairwise ordering fails. So NP can be destroyed by relabeling while the event sequence (ρ) is untouched! Exactly: NP is about correlations/order relations, ρ about sequence. Consistent with my gauge story: ρ preserved, NP not.
